title.sl: Vprašalni dodatki: isn't it? So do I
title.de: Frageanhängsel: isn't it? So do I
title.it: Le code interrogative: isn't it? So do I

goal.sl: Prosiš za pritrditev v vsakem času (It's cold, isn't it?, You saw him, didn't you?), pritrdiš (So do I, Neither can I) in odgovoriš na kratko (No, she hasn't).
goal.de: Du bittest um Zustimmung in jeder Zeit (It's cold, isn't it?, You saw him, didn't you?), stimmst zu (So do I, Neither can I) und antwortest kurz (No, she hasn't).
goal.it: Chiedi conferma in ogni tempo (It's cold, isn't it?, You saw him, didn't you?), sei d'accordo (So do I, Neither can I) e rispondi in breve (No, she hasn't).
goal.en: You can ask someone to agree in every tense (It's cold, isn't it?, You saw him, didn't you?), agree yourself (So do I, Neither can I), and give a short answer (No, she hasn't).

say.sl: **It's cold, isn't it?** Dodatek prosi sogovornika, naj pritrdi. (Mraz je, a ne?) Slovenščina ima za vse *a ne?*, angleščina vzame glagol iz stavka. Pritrdilni stavek, nikalni dodatek; nikalni stavek, pritrdilni dodatek: **It isn't far, is it?** **You're Jack's brother, aren't you?**
say.de: **It's cold, isn't it?** Der Anhang bittet den anderen um Zustimmung. (Es ist kalt, oder?) Deutsch hat für alles *oder?*, Englisch nimmt das Verb aus dem Satz. Bejahter Satz, verneinter Anhang; verneinter Satz, bejahter Anhang: **It isn't far, is it?** **You're Jack's brother, aren't you?**
say.it: **It's cold, isn't it?** La coda chiede all'altro di essere d'accordo. (Fa freddo, vero?) L'italiano ha per tutto *vero?*, l'inglese prende il verbo dalla frase. Frase positiva, coda negativa; frase negativa, coda positiva: **It isn't far, is it?** **You're Jack's brother, aren't you?**
say.en: **It's cold, isn't it?** A tag asks the other person to agree. It takes the verb from the sentence. A yes sentence, a no tag; a no sentence, a yes tag: **It isn't far, is it?** **You're Jack's brother, aren't you?**

examples.it: Sei il fratello di Jack, vero?

say.sl: **You live here, don't you?** Brez pomožnega glagola pride **do**, **does**, **did**. (Tu živiš, a ne?) **Jack works on the fell, doesn't he?** **You saw him, didn't you?** Nikalno: **You don't eat meat, do you?** V dodatku je vedno zaimek: Jack je he.
say.de: **You live here, don't you?** Ohne Hilfsverb kommt **do**, **does**, **did**. (Du wohnst hier, oder?) **Jack works on the fell, doesn't he?** **You saw him, didn't you?** Verneint: **You don't eat meat, do you?** Im Anhang steht immer ein Pronomen: Jack ist he.
say.it: **You live here, don't you?** Senza ausiliare viene **do**, **does**, **did**. (Abiti qui, vero?) **Jack works on the fell, doesn't he?** **You saw him, didn't you?** Negativo: **You don't eat meat, do you?** Nella coda c'è sempre un pronome: Jack è he.
say.en: **You live here, don't you?** With no helping verb, **do**, **does**, **did**. **Jack works on the fell, doesn't he?** **You saw him, didn't you?** With no: **You don't eat meat, do you?** The tag always has a pronoun: Jack is he.

say.sl: **It'll rain, won't it?** Drugi glagoli ostanejo: **have**, **will**, **can**, **was**. (Deževalo bo, a ne?) **You've been to Keswick, haven't you?** **She can swim, can't she?** **It was cold, wasn't it?** **He wasn't there, was he?** Pri **have** za to, kar imaš: **You've got a dog, haven't you?** **You have a dog, don't you?**
say.de: **It'll rain, won't it?** Andere Verben bleiben: **have**, **will**, **can**, **was**. (Es wird regnen, oder?) **You've been to Keswick, haven't you?** **She can swim, can't she?** **It was cold, wasn't it?** **He wasn't there, was he?** Bei **have** für Besitz: **You've got a dog, haven't you?** **You have a dog, don't you?**
say.it: **It'll rain, won't it?** Gli altri verbi restano: **have**, **will**, **can**, **was**. (Pioverà, vero?) **You've been to Keswick, haven't you?** **She can swim, can't she?** **It was cold, wasn't it?** **He wasn't there, was he?** Con **have** per ciò che possiedi: **You've got a dog, haven't you?** **You have a dog, don't you?**
say.en: **It'll rain, won't it?** The other helping verbs stay: **have**, **will**, **can**, **was**. **You've been to Keswick, haven't you?** **She can swim, can't she?** **It was cold, wasn't it?** **He wasn't there, was he?** With **have** for what you own: **You've got a dog, haven't you?** **You have a dog, don't you?**

say.sl: **I'm late, aren't I?** je za I am. (Zamujam, a ne?) Na Škotskem in Irskem rečejo tudi *amn't I*. **There's a bus, isn't there?** **Let's go, shall we?** **Close the door, will you?** **Nobody came, did they?** Ljudje rečejo tudi *innit*, v Walesu in Indiji *isn't it* za vse osebe; v pisanju je dodatek, ki se ujema. Glas pada: pričakuješ da. Glas se dvigne: res sprašuješ.
say.de: **I'm late, aren't I?** steht für I am. (Ich bin spät dran, oder?) In Schottland und Irland sagt man auch *amn't I*. **There's a bus, isn't there?** **Let's go, shall we?** **Close the door, will you?** **Nobody came, did they?** Man sagt auch *innit*, in Wales und Indien *isn't it* für alle Personen; geschrieben steht der passende Anhang. Stimme fällt: Du erwartest ein Ja. Stimme steigt: Du fragst wirklich.
say.it: **I'm late, aren't I?** è per I am. (Sono in ritardo, vero?) In Scozia e Irlanda si dice anche *amn't I*. **There's a bus, isn't there?** **Let's go, shall we?** **Close the door, will you?** **Nobody came, did they?** Si dice anche *innit*, in Galles e in India *isn't it* per tutti; per iscritto la coda che corrisponde. La voce scende: ti aspetti un sì. La voce sale: chiedi davvero.
say.en: **I'm late, aren't I?** is for I am. In Scotland and Ireland people also say *amn't I*. **There's a bus, isn't there?** **Let's go, shall we?** **Close the door, will you?** **Nobody came, did they?** People also say *innit*, and in Wales and India *isn't it* for every person; writing wants the tag that fits. Voice falling: you expect yes. Voice rising: you really ask.

say.sl: **So do I.** (Jaz tudi.) Pritrdiš pritrdilnemu: So + isti pomožni glagol + I: **I'm tired. — So am I.** **I was late. — So was I.** Pritrdiš nikalnemu: **Neither do I.** (Jaz tudi ne.) **I can't swim. — Neither can I.** Britanci rečejo tudi **Nor do I**. Ljudje rečejo tudi **Me too.** in **Me neither.**
say.de: **So do I.** (Ich auch.) Zustimmung zu einem Ja: So + dasselbe Hilfsverb + I: **I'm tired. — So am I.** **I was late. — So was I.** Zustimmung zu einem Nein: **Neither do I.** (Ich auch nicht.) **I can't swim. — Neither can I.** In Großbritannien auch **Nor do I**. Man sagt auch **Me too.** und **Me neither.**
say.it: **So do I.** (Anch'io.) D'accordo con un sì: So + lo stesso ausiliare + I: **I'm tired. — So am I.** **I was late. — So was I.** D'accordo con un no: **Neither do I.** (Nemmeno io.) **I can't swim. — Neither can I.** I britannici dicono anche **Nor do I**. Si dice anche **Me too.** e **Me neither.**
say.en: **So do I.** Agreeing with a yes: So + the same helping verb + I: **I'm tired. — So am I.** **I was late. — So was I.** Agreeing with a no: **Neither do I.** **I can't swim. — Neither can I.** The British also say **Nor do I**. People also say **Me too.** and **Me neither.**

say.sl: **Yes, I do.** **No, she hasn't.** Kratek odgovor vzame pomožni glagol iz vprašanja: **Has she gone? — No, she hasn't.** **Is it cold? — Yes, it is.** Pritrdilno brez krajšave: **Yes, it is.** Začudenje je kratko vprašanje: **I've been to Leeds. — Have you?** (Res?) **I don't drink tea. — Don't you?**
say.de: **Yes, I do.** **No, she hasn't.** Die Kurzantwort nimmt das Hilfsverb aus der Frage: **Has she gone? — No, she hasn't.** **Is it cold? — Yes, it is.** Beim Ja nicht verkürzt: **Yes, it is.** Staunen ist eine kurze Frage: **I've been to Leeds. — Have you?** (Wirklich?) **I don't drink tea. — Don't you?**
say.it: **Yes, I do.** **No, she hasn't.** La risposta breve prende l'ausiliare dalla domanda: **Has she gone? — No, she hasn't.** **Is it cold? — Yes, it is.** Con il sì senza forma breve: **Yes, it is.** Lo stupore è una domanda breve: **I've been to Leeds. — Have you?** (Davvero?) **I don't drink tea. — Don't you?**
say.en: **Yes, I do.** **No, she hasn't.** A short answer takes the helping verb from the question: **Has she gone? — No, she hasn't.** **Is it cold? — Yes, it is.** With yes, no short form: **Yes, it is.** Surprise is a short question: **I've been to Leeds. — Have you?** **I don't drink tea. — Don't you?**

exercises.text: — It's a lovely day, ___? — It is! You're staying at the inn, ___? — Yes. You don't know Mr Dixon, ___? — I do. He mended my gate. — I like walking. — So ___ I. — I've never been up Helvellyn. — ___ have I! — Let's go on Sunday, ___? — You can't come on Saturday, ___?

translation.sl: — Lep dan je, a ne? — Res je! Si v gostilni, a ne? — Ja. Gospoda Dixona ne poznaš, a ne? — Poznam ga. Popravil mi je vrata. — Rad{m:|f:a} hodim. — Jaz tudi. — Na Helvellynu še nikoli nisem bil{m:|f:a}. — Jaz tudi ne! — Greva v nedeljo, a? — V soboto ne moreš priti, a ne?
translation.de: — Ein schöner Tag, oder? — Ja! Du wohnst im Gasthaus, oder? — Ja. Du kennst Mr Dixon nicht, oder? — Doch. Er hat mein Tor repariert. — Ich gehe gern wandern. — Ich auch. — Ich war noch nie auf dem Helvellyn. — Ich auch nicht! — Gehen wir am Sonntag, ja? — Am Samstag kannst du nicht kommen, oder?
translation.it: — È una bella giornata, vero? — Sì! Alloggi alla locanda, vero? — Sì. Non conosci Mr Dixon, vero? — Sì che lo conosco. Mi ha riparato il cancello. — Mi piace camminare. — Anche a me. — Non sono mai salit{m:o|f:a} sull'Helvellyn. — Nemmeno io! — Andiamo domenica, va bene? — Sabato non puoi venire, vero?
translation.en: — It's a lovely day, isn't it? — It is! You're staying at the inn, aren't you? — Yes. You don't know Mr Dixon, do you? — I do. He mended my gate. — I like walking. — So do I. — I've never been up Helvellyn. — Neither have I! — Let's go on Sunday, shall we? — You can't come on Saturday, can you?

exercises.text: — You're Sam's sister, ___? — Yes. You've met him, ___? — I have. He doesn't live here, ___? — No, he lives by the brewery. — I don't like beer. — ___ do I! — There's a dance tonight, ___?

translation.sl: — Ti si Samova sestra, a ne? — Ja. Si ga že {m:spoznal|f:spoznala}, a ne? — Sem. Ne živi tu, a ne? — Ne, živi pri pivovarni. — Ne maram piva. — Jaz tudi ne! — Nocoj je ples, a ne?
translation.de: — Du bist Sams Schwester, oder? — Ja. Du hast ihn schon kennengelernt, oder? — Ja. Er wohnt nicht hier, oder? — Nein, er wohnt bei der Brauerei. — Ich mag kein Bier. — Ich auch nicht! — Heute Abend ist Tanz, oder?
translation.it: — Sei la sorella di Sam, vero? — Sì. L'hai già conosciuto, vero? — Sì. Non abita qui, vero? — No, abita vicino alla birreria. — La birra non mi piace. — Nemmeno a me! — Stasera c'è un ballo, vero?
translation.en: — You're Sam's sister, aren't you? — Yes. You've met him, haven't you? — I have. He doesn't live here, does he? — No, he lives by the brewery. — I don't like beer. — Neither do I! — There's a dance tonight, isn't there?
